title: Fractions, decimals and percents

primary_objective.statement: Change a fraction into a decimal by dividing, and change a decimal into a percent.

teach.text: A fraction is a division. The fraction 3/4 means 3 divided by 4. To change a fraction into a decimal, divide the top number (the numerator) by the bottom number (the denominator).
Some divisions never end. For example, 1 divided by 3 is 0.333… with the 3 repeating forever. When that happens, round to the number of decimal places you need.
Percent means "out of 100". To change a decimal into a percent, multiply it by 100. So 0.75 is 75%, and 0.4 is 40%.

examples.text: 1/3: divide 1 by 3. The answer is 0.333…, which is 0.33 rounded to two decimal places.

alternate_explanations.text: Imagine sharing 3 pizzas equally among 4 people. Each person gets 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75 of a pizza. That is the same amount as the fraction 3/4.

checks.feedback: 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6. Writing the digits side by side (0.35) or dividing 5 by 3 (1.67) are common mix-ups.

checks.prompt: Write 2/3 as a decimal, rounded to two decimal places.

return_cue: Back to your lesson: when you see a fraction, divide top by bottom. To show a decimal as a percent, multiply by 100.
